question:
Mad,
or mended?

beats.text: A grown man ran through Granada, crying out for mercy.
On the twentieth of January, 1537, he had heard John of Ávila preach.
beats.scene: Interior of a vast dark Spanish church at night: a tall carved stone pulpit lit by a hard shaft of light from a high window, a preacher in a plain dark cassock stands in it, seen from behind and far away, one arm raised; below him a packed crowd of small dark figures seen from behind, heads bowed. Skewed angular arches, drifting incense smoke. No faces.

beats.text: John was forty-two. He wept aloud, and beat his breast.
He gave away all he owned, and the city took him for mad.
They shut him in the Royal Hospital.
beats.scene: A long dark vaulted hospital ward of sixteenth-century Granada seen down its length: rows of bare iron-barred cell doors along both walls, one door slightly ajar with a thin bar of hard light on the stone floor, a single lantern hanging at the far end, mist on the floor. No people.

beats.text: One account says he was chained there, and beaten.
Then John of Ávila came to see him.
beats.scene: A small barred stone cell at night: a bent man in a worn cloak sits on straw against the far wall with his head bowed, tiny and in deep shadow; in the open doorway, a hooded preacher in a plain dark cassock stands with his back to the camera, a lantern in his hand throwing a long shaft of light across the floor toward the seated man. No faces.

beats.text: He told John to serve the poor, and not to punish himself.
